title: The Effects of Tai Chi on Insomnia: A Protocol for Randomized Controlled Trial
author: Jinying Li
materials: Insomnia is a prevalent clinical condition that is characterized by difficulties in either initiating or maintaining sleep, often leading to symptoms during waking hours, including fatigue, decreased attention span, impaired cognitive functioning, irritability, anxiety, and depressed mood. 1 The prevalence of insomnia is increasing worldwide, approximately 10-20% of adults in the United States suffer from insomnia. 2 In addition, the prevalence of insomnia in the Chinese population is as high as 45.4%. 3 Meanwhile, Insomnia can lead to changes in brain function, affecting mood regulation and even doubling the risk of future depression. 4,5 It can have a significant impact on an individual's overall well-being and quality of life, but this problem has not been effectively solved. A recently updated review suggests that the vulnerability to insomnia may exist in the brain circuits regulating emotion and arousal and speculated that in people with insomnia, the locus coeruleus (LC) is more sensitive to or receives more inputs from the salience network and related circuits. 6 Neuroimaging studies using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) indicate that insomnia amplifies activity within the “fear network”, which includes the salience network and the limbic system. 7-9 Furthermore, the anxiogenic impact of insomnia relates to impaired medial prefrontal cortex (PFC). 10 These findings collectively underscore the intricate interplay between brain regions involved in arousal, attention, emotional processing, and cognitive control, shedding light on how insomnia may impact these systems. Therefore, the abnormal functional state of brain connectivity signals can be used as a research target for insomnia. It is a breakthrough point to supplement and explain the neurobiological mechanism of insomnia. 11 The treatment of insomnia is divided into pharmacological and non-pharmacological therapy. However, prolonged medication usage may lead to drug resistance and dependency, while escalating doses and adverse effects can further impact the patient's health. 12 In addition, medication is not suitable for special populations (e.g., the elderly, pregnant women, and children). Cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBTI) is considered to be the gold standard in treating insomnia, which is expensive, labor intensive, and beyond the reach of many. 13 Novel non-invasive methods, such as transcranial direct current stimulation, transcranial magnetic stimulation, or auditory stimulation, lack sufficient evidence for clinical use in treating insomnia. 4 As a traditional non-pharmacological therapy in China, Tai Chi achieves co-regulation of emotion and arousal, improves high tonic LC discharge rates with high levels of arousal, and increases cognitive resources throughbilateral activation of the PFC under dual-tasking. 14,15 A recent study found that 3 months of Tai Chi was no worse than CBTI in improving sleep. 16 Importantly, Tai Chi enhances and activates functional brain connectivity, which can improve the quality of sleep in patients. 17,18 Thus, Tai Chi is a clinical option that is widely applicable, cost-effective, easy to perform, and has additional health benefits. With advances in neuroimaging technology, it is helping to reveal how insomnia affects brain function, thus providing a basis for the development of more effective therapeutic strategies. Using multimodal brain function analysis techniques such as resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS), this study provides an innovative approach to investigate how Tai Chi affects brain networks in insomnia, its therapeutic effects in different intervention cycles, and to clarify whether Tai Chi can replace CBTI as the preferred non-pharmacological therapy for insomnia.
Patients currently diagnosed with other mental disorders.

Statistical analysis SPSS26.0 statistical software was used for data analysis. The statistics and analysis of all data will be performed by an analytical researcher independent of the trial. Intention to treat (ITT) will be used for the main efficacy analysis and per protocol (PP) for the consistency test. The multiple imputation method will be the primary method for processing the missing data. Measurement data as mean ± standard deviation, using T-test, repeated measurement ANOVA, and non-parametric test methods such as Friedman analysis, The significance test was conducted by Mann-Whitney U test. All statistical tests will be performed on a two-sided test, and p ≤ 0.05 will be considered statistically significant.

steps.title: Recruit and Screen Participants
steps.instruction: Recruit 36 subjects (12 per group) from outpatients at the Sleep Medicine Center of West China Hospital Sichuan University, newspapers, social media, and advertising.

substeps.instruction: Obtain written informed consent from all participants.
Verify inclusion criteria: Meet DSM-5 criteria for insomnia disorder; aged 18-59 years; ISI score between 8 and 21 points; no disturbance of consciousness or intellectual impairment.

Verify exclusion criteria: Pregnancy/lactation; other mental disorders; severe sleep apnea, heart failure, myocardial infarction, stroke, tumor, severe lung disease, neurodegenerative disease, epilepsy, or restless leg syndrome; alcoholism or pill-popping; night shift/frequent cross-time zone travel; current insomnia treatment that cannot be stopped; use of psychotropic or sleep-affecting drugs in the month before enrollment; participation in other clinical trials within 1 month before enrollment.

steps.title: Randomize and Blind Participants
steps.instruction: Assign participants to one of three groups in a 1:1:1 ratio using a randomization sequence generated by SPSS 26.0.

substeps.instruction: Place randomly assigned sequences in consecutively numbered (1-36) sealed opaque envelopes.
Ensure envelopes are kept by a third party not involved in the study.
Blind statisticians, outcome assessors, and data analysts to group assignments.

steps.title: Implement Tai Chi Intervention
steps.instruction: Administer a 3-month program of 24-style simplified standard Yang's Tai Chi, consisting of two 1-hour sessions weekly.

substeps.instruction: Conduct introductory skills and focused teaching the week before the formal intervention, including demonstrations and precautions by a Chengdu Martial Arts College teacher and two assistants.
Structure each 1-hour session: 10 min warm-up, 45 min Tai Chi, and 5 min finishing activities.
Send course materials (breathing exercises, relaxation exercises, and 24-style Tai Chi videos) to subjects via WeChat for follow-up.

steps.title: Implement CBTI Intervention
steps.instruction: Administer a 3-month program of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia (CBTI), consisting of two 1-hour sessions weekly under the guidance of a trained therapist and two assistants.

substeps.instruction: Include stimulation control, sleep restriction, sleep hygiene, relaxation (diaphragmatic breathing, guided images), cognitive restructuring (thought diaries, behavioral experiments), and relapse prevention.
Hold weekly CBTI supervisory meetings to discuss cases and review recorded treatment processes.
Send all course materials to subjects via WeChat for follow-up.

steps.title: Implement Health Education Control
steps.instruction: Provide verbal health education and require recording of sleep twice a week for a total of 3 months.

steps.title: Perform fNIRS-based Feature Extraction
steps.instruction: Measure prefrontal cortex (PFC) activation during a dual-task test using a multi-channel continuous wave NIRScout fNIRS system (NIRx Medical Technologies, LLC) and 26-channel instruments (Wuhan Union Medical Technology Co).

substeps.instruction: Place the probe cap (16 light sources, 7 detectors, 3 cm spacing) on the PFC using the International 10–20 EEG system.
Set wavelengths to 670/830 nm and sampling frequency to 20Hz.

Execute the dual-task (Verbal Fluency Task and Emotional Sound Task) with a total duration of ~3.5 min: 30s baseline (counting 1-5), four 30s blocks (each consisting of 20s task and 10s break), and a 60s post-task period (counting 1-5).
Instruct subjects to form as many words as possible within 20s of hearing a Chinese word while receiving sound stimulation (happy, calm, fear, white noise).

Preprocess data using homer2 (MATLAB): apply band-pass filter (0.01-0.1 Hz), use a 30 dB threshold for noise, and remove motion artifacts via moving standard deviations and cubic spline interpolation.
Calculate HbO and HbR concentrations using the improved Beer-Lambert Law, using the last 10s of the pre-task break as the baseline.

steps.title: Perform rs-fMRI Feature Extraction
steps.instruction: Collect resting-state fMRI data using a 3.0 T whole-body MRI scanner (MAGNETOM-Skyra-SIEMENS) with a volume transmit head coil and 32-channel receive coil.

substeps.instruction: Acquire T1-weighted MRI: magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo sequence (TR/TE: 700 ms/11 ms, FOV: 256 × 256 × 192, voxel size: 1 × 1 × 0.9).
Acquire rs-fMRI: echo planar imaging (EPI) sequence (TR/TE/FA: 2020 ms/30 ms/90°, FOV: 106 × 106 × 46, voxel size: 2.4 × 2.4 × 3.75, duration: 200 TR).
Exclude participants who fell asleep during the scan.

Preprocess data using DPARSF and SPM8 on MATLAB: remove first 10 images, perform slice timing and realignment (max displacement/rotation < 2.0 mm), spatially normalize to MNI template, re-sample to 3 mm, apply 4-mm Gaussian kernel smoothing, remove linear trend, and filter (0.01-0.1 Hz).
Perform regressions on Friston 24 head movement model, white matter, CSF signal, and overall signal.
Define LC seed region as a sphere (radius 3 mm) at MNI coordinates (x = −14; y = −34; z = −28) and calculate voxel-wise FC maps.

steps.title: Assess Sleep and Anxiety Indicators
steps.instruction: Evaluate participants using standardized scales at 4, 8, and 12 weeks, and at a 4-week follow-up.

substeps.instruction: Administer Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) to assess sleep quality (range 0–21).
Administer Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) to assess nighttime and daytime symptoms.
Administer Hamilton Anxiety Scale (HAMA) to assess physical and psychological anxiety.

steps.title: Monitor Safety and Adverse Events
steps.instruction: Monitor insomnia severity via subjective measurements during treatment and at 3-month follow-up.

substeps.instruction: Immediately suspend experimental sessions if moderate-to-severe side effects occur (e.g., headaches, insomnia, acute mood changes).
Encourage reporting of all adverse events; have psychiatrists evaluate if events are associated with the intervention.
